analysis.title: Home Depot and Lowe's F3Q26 Read-Throughs
key_insights: HD US comps rose 2.2% YOY in F3Q26 vs +0.1% in F3Q25, with 13 of 16 departments positive. LOW comps rose 1.8% YOY vs +0.4% in F3Q25, with 7 of 13 categories positive.
Demand was led by maintenance and small-ticket repair. GS says the rise in mortgage rates above 7% and macro uncertainty are producing greater-than-expected weakness into year-end.
Average ticket grew 3.0% at HD (split evenly between SKU-level price and intra-category mix) and 3.5% at LOW. HD transactions fell 0.5% and LOW transactions fell 1.7%.

Raw material costs are rising, including transportation, oil-based inputs such as resins, and key commodities. Manufacturers are raising prices to offset them. GS models price/mix gains for most companies in its coverage this year.
HD big-ticket transactions (over $1,000) grew 4.5% YOY vs +2.4% last quarter, led by appliances and portable power.

Pro comps outpaced DIY at both retailers. At HD, pro strength came in water heaters, insulation (OC) and siding (LPX). At LOW, it came in rough plumbing including water heaters (AOS), electrical and lumber.

Appliances (WHR) were strong at both retailers: LOW had its eighth consecutive quarter of positive appliance comps, the strongest since 2021. This contrasts with WHR's own 3Q commentary and 4Q guide, which GS attributes to consumers choosing to fix rather than replace.
HD monthly US comps: +1.1% in August, +4.4% in September (helped by favorable weather), +1.3% in October. LOW monthly comps: +0.3%, +2.9%, +2.0%.
HD now expects F2026 comps slightly above the unchanged ~1.4% midpoint. LOW guided to ~0.5% growth, up from flat.

SRS (HD) saw positive comps despite roofing weakness from the lack of severe weather. It is now expected to grow low-single digits in F2026, down from mid-single digits. HD plans 40-50 new branches. LOW plans 15 new FBM branches.
GS highlights Buy-rated FBIN, MAS, MHK and TREX as best positioned for company-specific initiatives and relative outperformance.
LOW said favorable October weather continued into November, extending the outdoor selling season. GS reads this as upside to 4Q sales for TREX, LPX, POOL and SITE.
Lumber comps were positive at both retailers, helped by higher commodity prices. GS expects recent capacity reductions to support pricing, partly offset by weaker housing activity.

OC: industry roofing shingle shipments fell 13% YOY in 3Q after +0.2% in 2Q, which GS attributes partly to pull-forward. OC expects segment revenue to decline high-single digits, with channel de-stock through 1Q.

market_movers.rationale: Faucets outperformed at Home Depot, and Moen and House of Rohl have launched new products in the last ~6 months. GS lists FBIN among the best-positioned Buy-rated names. Rating and price ($47.21) are from the disclosure section.

Plumbing and paint outperformed as consumers focus on small repair projects. Delta and Behr were recognized at HD's supplier meeting. HD is 38% of 2025 sales and LOW under 10%. Rating and price ($84.33) are from the disclosure section.
Named among the Buy-rated names best positioned. The report gives no company-specific read-through. Price $148.44 is from the disclosure section.
LOW reported an extended outdoor selling season from favorable October weather continuing into November, which GS sees as upside to 4Q sales. Price $52.26 is from the disclosure section.

Appliance comps were strong at both retailers, in contrast to WHR's weak 3Q results and 4Q guide. WHR cited retail price up high-single digits vs January 2025 and a further 7% increase effective early December. GS estimates appliance industry shipments will fall 3.4% this year.
Insulation strength at HD is positive, but roofing shingle shipments fell 13% YOY in 3Q. OC expects segment revenue to decline high-single digits with channel de-stock through 1Q.

Water heaters were strong at LOW and HD. AOS guided to a low-single-digit decline in 2026 residential industry volumes, with wholesale weak and retail firm. It announced a price increase of up to 9.5% effective in December.
Siding was a pro strength category at HD. 3Q sell-through of ExpertFinish was +8% YOY and +13% sequentially.
HVAC and replacement sales contributed to LOW's rough plumbing comps. CSW saw volume and price expansion in Contractor Solutions in F2Q, and 75% of segment sales are R&R-driven.
Lumber comps were positive at both retailers, helped by higher commodity prices. Housing activity is expected to weaken in coming quarters.

sector_views.rationale: Repair and maintenance activity leads sales while consumers defer larger discretionary and financed projects. Mortgage rates above 7% and macro uncertainty are weighing into year-end. GS expects these pressures to persist and favors company-specific initiatives.

earnings_insights: HD F3Q26 US comps +2.2% YOY (reported) vs +0.1% in F3Q25. LOW F3Q26 comps +1.8% YOY (reported) vs +0.4% in F3Q25.
HD F2026 comp guidance: slightly above the unchanged ~1.4% midpoint (company guidance). LOW F2026 guidance: ~0.5% growth, up from flat (company guidance).
SRS is expected to grow low-single digits in F2026, down from mid-single digits (HD management expectation, reported on the F3Q call).
OC expects segment revenues to decline high-single digits, led by volume, with channel de-stock through 1Q (company expectation).
AOS guided to a low-single-digit decline in 2026 residential industry volumes (company guidance). WHR 3Q results and 4Q guide were weak (previously reported).

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS says the spike above 7% is contributing to greater-than-expected weakness in building products into year-end, as consumers defer larger financed projects.
GS's own estimate. Retail appliance demand is stronger than this implies, with consumers repairing rather than replacing.
Weak because of the lack of severe weather and pull-forward from 2Q (+0.2% YOY).

risk_factors: Mortgage rates above 7% and macro uncertainty are pressuring consumers' appetite for larger-ticket and financed projects.
Rising raw material, oil-based input and transportation costs. Price increases could weigh on volumes.
Weak housing activity expected in coming quarters, partly offsetting lumber price support.
Lack of severe weather weighs on roofing and shingle demand.
Appliance mix pressure as consumers shift to fix vs replace and stay within budgets.
Channel de-stock in roofing and insulation through 1Q.

tension_points.bull_case: HD and LOW both reported strong appliance comps. LOW had its eighth straight quarter of positive comps, the strongest since 2021, supported by fulfillment, assortment and delivery investments.
tension_points.bear_case: WHR's own 3Q results and 4Q guide were weak, and GS estimates 2026 appliance industry shipments will contract 3.4% as consumers repair rather than replace and mix is pressured.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further WHR guide-down, or retailer appliance comps turning negative after the holiday period, since GS says it will monitor activity over the holiday.
